title: Embedding traffic demultiplexer + proactive capacity forecast for mixed embeddings/rerank workloads
creator: Maya Kapoor
description:
Background:
We operate mixed traffic (short, high-concurrency embedding calls and occasional larger reranking jobs) on the same embedding fleet. Current blunt autoscaler and global token-based rate limits are causing two repeated problems: (1) noisy-tenants trigger headroom drain leading to p95/p99 latency spikes for other tenants; (2) rerank bursts (many long sequences) cause eviction of warm KV caches and transient tail latency regressions.

Goal:
Design and implement a traffic demultiplexer + proactive short-horizon capacity forecast that: (A) isolates reranking-like requests (longer seqs, higher GPU time) from short embedding requests using inexpensive classification heuristics at ingress; (B) pre-provisions ephemeral headroom for predicted bursts using a 5–30 minute forecast; (C) expose per-tenant burst-credit buckets and fair admission to avoid noisy-tenant starvation. Targets: reduce embedding p95 by 25% in mixed workloads, avoid >3x latency regressions during rerank storms, and keep cost delta <6% for steady-state.

Design summary:
1) Ingress demultiplexer: lightweight rule engine at the embedding router that tags requests as SHORT (<=512 tokens, embedding-only), LONG (>=512 tokens or rerank flag), and MIXED (embedding+rerank pipeline). Rules first-class: request.body.length_tokens, request.headers.x-rerank, client.provided_hint. The router sends SHORT traffic to optimized hot pools with small KV caches, LONG to a separate long-job queue backed by GPU slices that tolerate batching at higher latency.

2) Short-horizon forecasting: combine EWMA of recent qps (1m/5m) with a seasonality term (time-of-day) and a lightweight L2 regressor for tenants that repeatedly burst. Forecast horizon: 1, 5, 15, 30 minutes. Output: predicted token rate per tenant & model variant.

3) Burst-credit system: each tenant accrues credits based on steady-state commitment (reserved capacity) and recent usage; credits allow short bursts without immediate autoscaler action. Credits decay on admission and refill over configurable windows.

4) Autoscaler integration: the forecast feeds a proactive-scaler which can pre-warm small ephemeral instances or reassign spare hot-pool slots. The existing autoscaler remains as fallback. Autoscaler policy changes are feature-gated.

5) Fair admission & soft-shaping: when capacity tight, system first applies per-tenant soft-shape based on credits, then global tail-drop. Short requests get priority lanes for 95th-latency SLO.

Metrics and measurements to capture:
- baseline: p50/p95/p99 token latency for SHORT and LONG buckets, KV cache hit rate, cold-start frequency, tokens/sec per-GPU.
- target: p95 reduction 25% for SHORT in mixed loads, <2% requests retried due to preemption, cost increase <6% steady-state.
- telemetry: per-tenant forecast error (MAPE), credit utilization, pre-warm failure rate.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end: under a synthetic mixed workload (10 steady tenants + 2 bursty tenants producing 5x bursts), observed SHORT p95 reduced by >=25% and LONG request median latency within 1.2x baseline.
- Operational: dashboards showing forecast vs actual, credit burn-down, and autoscaler pre-warm success metrics.
- Rollout: feature-gate opt-in for 10% of tenants, with automatic rollback for regressed latency or error spikes.

Implementation plan (high level):
Week 1: build ingress demultiplexer prototype + unit tests.
Week 2: implement forecast service (binary: ewma+seasonality) and expose per-tenant predictions via internal API.
Week 3: implement burst-credit accounting and admission logic in router (no autoscaler changes yet).
Week 4: integrate proactive-scaler hooks (pre-warm requests) and safe fallbacks.
Week 5: internal canary with synthetic load, iterate.
Week 6: 10% customer opt-in, monitor 2 weeks, then roll to 50% if metrics good.

Safety & rollback:
- All new routing decisions are reversible via opt-out header and runtime feature flag.
- Autoscaler hooks are additive: if pre-warm fails, fallback to existing autoscaler.
- Monitoring alarms: composite alert if SHORT p95 increases >15% vs baseline after rollout.

Config example (ingress rules, as YAML for clarity):

rules:
  - name: rerank-detect
    condition: "request.headers.x-rerank == \"1\" or request.body.tokens > 512"
    action: route_long
  - name: short-default
    condition: "else"
    action: route_short

burst_credit_default:
  steady_refill_per_min: 0.5
  max_credits: 10
  emergency_buffer: 2

forecast_params:
  horizons: [1m,5m,15m,30m]
  ewma_alpha: 0.25
  seasonality_enabled: true

Capacity calc example:
- Baseline steady tokens/sec per-GPU = 1200 tokens/s
- Observed short-traffic steady: 80k tokens/s -> 67 GPUs (80k / 1200)
- Predicted short 5m burst: +40k tokens/s -> need 33 extra GPUs; proactive pre-warm targets 25–40% of that depending on budget (we pick 30% -> 10 GPUs pre-warmed)

Runbook notes:
- If pre-warm fails repeatedly (>3 times in 10 minutes) for a tenant, throttle that tenant's burst credit and notify SEs.
- If SHORT p95 regresses >20%, disable demux for that region and escalate.
